assessment: The LLM now chooses approved article passages and follow-up questions while the server preserves role restrictions. Exact source wording removed invented factual advice in the final tests; conversational usefulness remains uneven.
changes: The existing Qwen model interprets real conversation history, bounded memory, corrections and parent goals to select relevant approved guidance.
Factual guidance is rendered directly from canonical article passages, including scope, conditions and citations. Generated factual prose cannot enter the response.
The model chooses a natural clarification from eight bounded question types. A second model call checks passage applicability, with at most one repair.
Server-owned profiles, explicit role grants, course boundaries and fresh indexed metadata checks remain authoritative. A remembered article cannot bypass current authorization.
Unconfirmed Moodle access methods/platforms require clarification. Narrow coverage checks return an honest gap for unsupported PIN, automatic-denial and failed-recovery-page procedures.
remaining_findings: Seven of nineteen final conversations passed; twelve were partial. No invented factual guidance or unauthorized source exposure was observed in these cases, but quoting faithfully does not guarantee a relevant answer.
Enrollment progression can skip View or fall back after an explicit screen report. CAC recovery sometimes repeats general guidance instead of the next actionable step.
Some correct answers are rejected by the model reviewer, causing generic fallbacks, including role-sensitive help and a direct form-submission question.
Whole bullet lists are offered as a single passage, so focused course-action questions can receive lengthy lists and repeated source introductions.
An explicit course switch can be blocked by a historical course mention. The manual-unlock case quoted a before-wait section after the user reported waiting.
Phone method clarification, browser/app corrections, PIN coverage limits, Moodle recovery/resume and held-out username recovery worked in the final tests.
limitations: This is a bounded synthetic text API evaluation, not a claim of general accuracy. Sixteen conversations replay earlier fixed inputs; three new two-turn cases use adaptive follow-ups. Calls were serialized against the real VM app and Qwen model. Browser interaction, screenshots, concurrent users and unseen articles were not evaluated. Role selection remains a demo identity, not production authentication.

additional_smoke_checks.note: Separate targeted smoke calls are excluded from the 54-turn replay. One final role-help smoke response was a safe but unhelpful fallback.

review_notes: Grades assess usefulness and applicability as well as source fidelity; zero fail grades does not mean every turn was useful.
A model review acceptance is not proof of correctness. Traces were independently checked for source-access consistency.
Known coverage guards are narrow wording checks, not an exhaustive unsupported-request classifier.
